key_insight: Trigonal selenium appears intrinsically defect tolerant: even though point defects create deep gap states, they do not efficiently drive Shockley-Read-Hall recombination because large lattice reorganization and energy losses suppress both nonradiative and radiative capture.
engineering_relevance: This makes trigonal selenium a promising wide-band-gap absorber for tandem and indoor photovoltaics, with defect engineering likely less critical than in many other emerging materials.
method: First-principles calculations of a large, chemically diverse set of point defects in trigonal selenium
Evaluation of defect-assisted Shockley-Read-Hall recombination through nonradiative multi-phonon emission and radiative capture channels
Assessment of how defect level position, lattice relaxation, charge state, and doping conditions affect recombination rates
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that across realistic defect concentrations, SRH recombination is too weak to explain the observed efficiency losses in selenium photovoltaics.
watch_item: The conclusion is based on computed defect physics; practical device performance still depends on microstructure, synthesis control, interfaces, and extrinsic degradation pathways not covered here.
paper_title: Defect Tolerance in Trigonal Selenium Photovoltaics
